data.title: Home Services
data.summary: A Raspberry Pi backend for camera recording, file recovery and secure handoffs between Apple apps.
data.oneLiner: A Raspberry Pi backend for camera recording, file recovery and secure handoffs between Apple apps.

caseStudy.problem: A Mac can sleep or disconnect while cameras, backups and mobile workflows still need an always-available endpoint.
caseStudy.role: I designed and deployed the service contracts, Raspberry Pi runtime and Mac status tooling.
architecture: Camera Monitor and Files & Backups can use a versioned API on the Pi with scoped tokens.
Private relays can queue selected editorial and opportunity edits for a Mac. The Chew Sense mailbox accepts encrypted recording deposits.
decisions: Keep the camera and file apps usable with their direct providers. Separate status, write access and publication permissions.
validation: Camera and file provider adapters have been exercised against the deployed Pi. The encrypted recording mailbox is deployed.

readme.content:
# Home Services

[Public source and tests](https://github.com/ZSturman/Home-Services-Public)

A small server runs continuously on a Raspberry Pi. It handles managed camera recordings, backup status and recovery, and selected app handoffs. The Mac status console shows disk space, schedules and recent jobs.

Mobile clients use scoped access for the services they need. When the Mac is asleep, the Pi can hold selected edits or encrypted captures for later processing. Publication and other source-owned decisions stay with the apps that own them.

The architecture diagram shows how the apps connect to this private deployment.
